title: Progress and Impact of Proposed Workplace Fairness Legislation and Support Measures Available
what_it_is: Progress and Impact of Proposed Workplace Fairness Legislation and Support Measures Available

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Legislation questions
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Manpower about the Workplace Fairness Legislation's progress, support for SMEs, and recourse for employees of small firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether he can provide an update on the progress of the proposed Workplace Fairness Legislation; and (b) when considering the proposed legislation, whether the Ministry will take into account (i) plans to mitigate any negative impact, (ii) how employees can seek help and (iii) the impact on the employer-employee relationship.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: asked 	the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry will provide SMEs with additional support measures to ensure that they are compliant with fair employment best practices and processes; and (b) if so, what are they.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower given that firms with fewer than 25 employees are exempted from the Workplace Fairness Legislation, what recourse will employees of such firms have when faced with workplace discrimination.

sections.label: Workplace discrimination complaint numbers
sections.summary: Workplace discrimination complaints have fallen, but TAFEP and MOM still received about 315 complaints a year over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To Mr Seah Kian Peng's question, over the years, the number of workplace discrimination complaints has, in fact, fallen, but the Tripartite Alliance for Fair Employment Practices (TAFEP) and MOM still received about 315 complaints of discrimination a year over the last five years.

sections.label: Retaliation protection and small firm exemption
sections.summary: There will be protection against retaliation for reporting discrimination, and the Committee recommends exempting firms with fewer than 25 employees for a start.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To ensure that employees who experience discrimination feel assured to come forward to report it, there will also be protection against retaliation for making a complaint of discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: As Ms Yeo Wan Ling, Mr Edward Chia and Mr Sharael Taha have pointed out, small firms may lack the expertise or resources to fully implement the legislated requirements from the get-go.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Therefore, the Committee recommends exempting small firms with fewer than 25 employees from the legislation for a start, with a view to lowering this exemption in five years.

sections.label: Committee deliberations and legislation timeline
sections.summary: Breastfeeding protection and reasonable accommodations are still being considered, with final recommendations targeted for later this year and legislation ready in the second half of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To Mr Louis Ng's question on protection for women who are breastfeeding, and Ms He Ting Ru's question on reasonable accommodations, these are matters that the Committee is still considering.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Sharael Taha's questions on the timeline, the Committee targets to complete its deliberations and release its final recommendations in the later part of this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Thereafter, drafting of the legislation will commence and we aim for that to be ready in the second half of 2024.

sections.label: Penalties and protected characteristics
sections.summary: When sex is included as a protected characteristic, the legislation will look into protecting pregnant and postpartum women.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: On the second question of whether we can strengthen penalties under the guidelines, let me just say that when the protected characteristics of sex were included in the new legislation, it will look into how we can protect maybe women who are pregnant as well as perhaps in the postpartum period as well.

sections.label: Graded penalties for discrimination offences
sections.summary: Penalties in the legislation will be graded towards the level of egregiousness of the offence and discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Currently, there are penalties that will be included in the legislation will be graded towards the level of egregiousness of that particular offence and discrimination.

sections.label: Employer insufficient documentation
sections.summary: Insufficient documentation by the employer may be taken against the employer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In the instance where the employer has insufficient documentation, that may be taken against the employer.

sections.label: 315 complaints across company sizes
sections.summary: The speaker lacks an exact breakdown of 315 complaints by company size but says they span varying sizes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: When I mentioned that there are 315 complaints, I do not have the exact breakdown of the complaints by company sizes, but I would say that complaints like these do span across companies of varying sizes as well.

sections.label: Safeguards against retaliation
sections.summary: Legislation should include safeguards against retaliation for employees or workers who report discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: One of the things we want to prevent and encourage people who faced discrimination to come forward to report is to make sure that when they do report a case of discrimination, whether as a victim or as a fellow worker who witnessed any form of discrimination, is to make sure that, in the legislation, we put in place safeguards against retaliation against these employees or workers who raise issues of discrimination.
